fixtures.basis: Kansas has no statewide code, so the Unified Building and Trade Code sets the counts. It reprints Table 2902.1 of the 2024 International Building Code with local footnotes and rewrites Sections 2902.2, 2902.3, 2902.4 and 2902.6; the Uniform Plumbing Code's Table 422.1 is excluded. The rows for offices, restaurants and schools equal the model 2024 rows (read on page images of the county's PDF, pages 85 to 86). Section 2902.1.1 (half men, half women; round up) is not amended and was read on UpCodes' Wichita-Sedgwick copy.

amendment.text: (1) Footnote g: each urinal may replace one of the required men's toilets, but toilets may not fall below half of the number specified, in every occupancy (the Uniform Plumbing Code's urinal rules are excluded, and the model 67% for assembly and schools does not appear). (2) Separate rooms for each sex are not required where 25 or fewer people are employed (owner's letter or a statement on the plans), or in a dining or drinking establishment with 25 seats or fewer and an assembly area of 735 square feet or less; the model exceptions for 15 or fewer occupants, business occupancies of 25 or fewer and mercantile of 100 or fewer are replaced. (3) Rooms for all persons regardless of sex may replace separate rooms where privacy is provided under Uniform Plumbing Code Sections 422.6 and 422.7. (4) Footnote d: seasonal outdoor seating above 16 occupants counts toward the fixtures. (5) Footnote a: one fixture for the number of persons indicated 'or any fraction'.
amendment.quote: g. Where urinals are provided, one water closet less than the number specified may be provided for each urinal installed, except the number of water closets in such cases shall not be reduced to less than one half of the minimum specified. [...] [P] 2902.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: [...] 2. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces where 25 or fewer are employed. A letter from the owner or a statement on the architectural plans attesting to the maximum number of employees is sufficient documentation. 3. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilet rooms are provided in accordance with Section 2902.1.2. 4. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 422.6 of the Uniform Plumbing Code and for urinals in accordance with Section 422.7 of the Uniform Plumbing Code. 5. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required for dining and/or drinking establishments when the seating capacity is 25 or less and the overall assembly is 735 square feet (68 m2) or less.

table_rows.split_rounding_quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
table_rows.all_gender_count_quote: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.
table_rows.footnote_a_quote: a. The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.

worked_examples.how: 25 each. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 1 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 1, so up to 0 urinals.
50 each. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 2 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 2, so up to 1 urinal.
100 each. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 3, so up to 1 urinal.
200 each. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 5, so up to 2 urinals.
25 each. 25/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 1, so up to 0 urinals.
50 each. 50/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 1, so up to 0 urinals.
100 each. 100/75 rounds up to 2 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 2, so up to 1 urinal.
200 each. 200/75 rounds up to 3 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 3, so up to 1 urinal.
25 each. 25/50 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 1, so up to 0 urinals.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 1, so up to 0 urinals.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 2, so up to 1 urinal.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals (footnote g): toilets may not drop below half of 4, so up to 2 urinals.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Toilet counts equal the state pack's model figures; the urinal allowance differs (restaurant at 400: 1, not 2). Urinals are optional, never required. For 3 toilets, 'not less than one half' is read as at least 2 toilets (1 urinal); for 5, at least 3 (2 urinals).

restrooms_city.rule: No separate city ordinance was found. The Unified Building and Trade Code sets three rules: (1) single-user and family toilet rooms must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex (2024 IBC Section 2902.1.2, not amended); (2) a room designed for all persons regardless of sex may replace separate rooms where privacy for toilets and urinals meets the plumbing code (Section 2902.2 exception 4 as amended); (3) required public toilet facilities need a sign, near the entrance, saying whether the room is for males, females or all persons (Section 2902.4 as amended). Kansas's 2026 law on government buildings (state pack) sits above these for public buildings.
restrooms_city.quote: [P] 2902.4 Signage. Required public toilet facilities shall be provided with signs that indicate whether the facility is to be used by males, by females, or by all persons regardless of sex. Signs shall be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility. Signs for accessible toilet facilities shall comply with the provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act ("ADA"). [...] [2902.1.2, UpCodes copy] Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.
restrooms_city.note: Section 2902.2 exception 4 points to Uniform Plumbing Code Sections 422.6 and 422.7 for privacy; those sections were not read (UpCodes' copy of the 2021 UPC chapter did not load its text). One web search found no Wichita ordinance on restroom signs; the Code of the City of Wichita on Municode was not searched (blocks automated access).

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Wichita job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Wichita and Sedgwick County rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Wichita aircraft plants, schools, hospitals and offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and Kansas law makes the federal rules state law without adding its own. Kansas has no state review of plans for access in private buildings. In Wichita the Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department (MABCD), the building department the city shares with Sedgwick County, checks it.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Wichita's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) used as an interior finish to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Wichita sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and lets urinals take the place of up to half of the men's toilets. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Access rules in Wichita:** Wichita's building rules say buildings must be designed to the current federal access guidelines. Inside the city limits, Wichita also applies them to private clubs and religious buildings, which the federal rules leave out.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Wichita's building rules a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone, and a shared all-gender room may take the place of separate men's and women's rooms where the toilets and urinals have the privacy the plumbing rules call for. Every required public restroom needs a sign near its entrance saying whether it is for men, for women or for everyone. In buildings owned or leased by a government body, a Kansas law in force since February 2026 requires every restroom built for more than one person to be designated for one sex. One-person and family restrooms are still allowed there.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Wichita requires a permit to alter a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets and "similar finish work", and partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high that are not fixed and can be moved, but it doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask MABCD at 316-660-1840 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department (MABCD)
page.stalls_intro: Kansas has no statewide building rules, so the rules Wichita shares with Sedgwick County decide. They count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: each urinal may take the place of one men's toilet, up to half of them in any kind of building, and each urinal needs a screen. The table shows men's toilets as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A building or tenant space where 25 or fewer people are employed doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Neither does a restaurant or bar with 25 seats or fewer and an assembly area of 735 square feet or less. Confirm the count with MABCD.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Wichita's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or MABCD sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Wichita and Sedgwick County license general contractors through MABCD, in Classes A to D. The licensing rules don't apply to a subcontractor working under a general contractor, or to a nonstructural job that costs $2,500 or less. Kansas has no state license for this work. Confirm what your project needs with MABCD. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor in Wichita needs a license from the Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department, except on a nonstructural job of $2,500 or less or when working under a general contractor.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Kansas has no state wage law for public construction, and state law bars cities and counties from setting wage rates for construction contractors, so set wage rates apply only on federally funded jobs. For a carpenter on building work in Sedgwick County the federal rate is $17.62 an hour plus $1.93 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Wichita: 6.5% state and 1% Sedgwick County. Wichita has no city sales tax. Some addresses, several of them downtown, sit in special districts that add 1% to 2%.
page.buyers_extra: - **Aircraft plants and their suppliers:** HDPE or phenolic in shop-floor restrooms and locker rooms, powder coated steel or laminate in the office areas.

notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a permit in Wichita, since the exempt list names only 'nonfixed and movable' partitions and 'similar finish work' (MABCD, 316-660-1840; Commercial Building Plan Review Supervisor, 316-660-1798).

The unamended parts of the code (half men and half women, rounding up, single-user restroom signs, stalls and urinal screens, floor area per person, the HDPE fire-test section) were read on UpCodes' Wichita-Sedgwick copy, not on ICC's site: check once in a browser.
The fire-test section says 'used as an interior finish' and doesn't name toilet partitions (same wording as other cities' pages).
City of Wichita Ordinance 52-564 (the city's side of the 2024 building code adoption) could not be opened (403); the county's Resolution 205-2024 and the MABCD pages were read instead.
The all-gender room rule points to two plumbing code sections (Uniform Plumbing Code 422.6 and 422.7) for privacy, which were not read; the page only says 'the privacy the plumbing rules call for'.

A 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code adoption appears to be under review by MABCD's plumbing board (search-result summaries of 2025 and 2026 board agendas, not opened); the codes page still lists the 2021 edition. Recheck before launch.

School column: Kansas school buildings also come under K.S.A. 31-150 and the State Fire Marshal's edition of the building code; ask MABCD or the State Fire Marshal (785-296-3401) which sets toilet counts in a K-12 school.
